slides.title: Pacing and cut on action
slides.source: Source: Shipping Lane SHOTLIST.md; trailer-craft.md; "cut on action" is general film vocabulary.
slides.notes: Shot lengths are the nine Shipping Lane shots. The jump uses speed 24 px a frame across, 40 up, gravity 3.4 px a frame squared (invented inputs).
slides.picture: Step one shows nine shots with their cuts per minute rising from 20 to 30. Step two shows a jump arc with three possible cut points and the speed at each.

new_texts: How fast the cuts come; it follows how well the viewer understands the game.
Shortest shot 1.5 s; the gate's floor is 0.8 s.
Pacing is cuts per minute. It rises toward the peak, but only after the viewer knows the game: 20 to 25.7 to 30 here.
all_texts: How fast the cuts come; it follows how well the viewer understands the game.
Shortest shot 1.5 s; the gate's floor is 0.8 s.
Pacing is cuts per minute. It rises toward the peak, but only after the viewer knows the game: 20 to 25.7 to 30 here.

new_texts: Cut while the motion is under way, so the eye carries across the cut.
A before the jump: speed 0.0 px a frame
B at the apex: speed 24.0 px a frame
C 2 frames after takeoff: speed 41.0 px a frame
A cut hides best when the eye is already following motion. Cut at C, not A or B, and the move carries across.

slides.title: Before a trailer goes out
slides.source: Source: godot-trailer SKILL.md and trailer-craft.md (the one test and the viewer test).
slides.picture: A checklist of six items drawn one at a time.

new_texts: Does real gameplay show in the first five seconds?
Can I say the hook in one sentence?
Is every shot readable, and are the cuts on the beat?
Is every shot real play from this build?
Does it work with the sound off, with no rapid flashing?
One call to action, held long enough to read?
Then say it exactly: not “make it exciting”, but “1.5 s shots into the peak”.
